I am an old woman of 71 years, farming this small rented plot of cassava and cocoyam here in the South East. My children help me sometimes but my back is not what it used to be, so I must work slowly and carefully. I cannot afford much chemical fertilizer on rented land — I will put a little NPK when the rains come well, and I always spread the household refuse and goat droppings on the mounds. I plant the cassava cuttings from my sister's farm like we always do, and with the yam and cocoyam mixed in, the weeds are my biggest worry, not pests.
